spots.name: Petrovaradin Fortress
spots.summary: Petrovaradin Fortress, nicknamed "Gibraltar on/of the Danube", is a bastion fortress in the town of Petrovaradin, itself part of the City of Novi Sad, Serbia. It is located on the right bank of the Danube river.

spots.name: Name of Mary Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Name of Mary Church is a Roman Catholic church in Novi Sad, Serbia, dedicated to the feast of the Most Holy Name of the Blessed Virgin Mary. Commonly known as the Cathedral, it is the largest church in Novi Sad, located on the central Freedom Square.

spots.name: Saint George Cathedral, Novi Sad

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Saint George the Great Martyr Cathedral, is an Eastern Orthodox church located in Novi Sad, Serbia. It is under jurisdiction of the Eparchy of Bačka of the Serbian Orthodox Church and serves as its cathedral church.

spots.name: Novi Sad Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Novi Sad Synagogue is a former Neolog Jewish congregation and synagogue, located in downtown Novi Sad, Serbia. Completed in 1909, the building was used as a synagogue until 1966 and repurposed to a cultural center since 2012.

spots.name: Bishop's Palace, Novi Sad

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Bishop's Palace is the seat and bishop's palace of the Eparchy of Bačka of the Serbian Orthodox Church, located in Novi Sad, Serbia. The building is listed as the Cultural Heritage Site of Exceptional Importance.

spots.name: Novi Sad City Hall
spots.summary: The Novi Sad City Hall or the Magistrate is a neo-renaissance building housing the municipal institutions of Novi Sad, the capital of the autonomous province of Vojvodina, Serbia. Due to its heritage value, it is listed as a protected cultural monument of the Republic of Serbia.

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Museum of Vojvodina is an art and natural history museum in Novi Sad, Serbia. The museum houses a collection of over 400,000 specimens and a library of over 50,000 volumes.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Nikolajevska Church, officially the Serbian Orthodox Church of the Translation of the Relics of Saint Nicholas, is an 18th-century Serbian Orthodox church in Novi Sad, Serbia.

spots.name: Danube Park
spots.summary: Danube Park or Dunavski Park is an urban park in the downtown of Novi Sad, the capital of the Vojvodina Province, Serbia. Formed in 1895, it is protected as the natural monument and is one of the symbols of the city.

spots.name: Banovina Palace
spots.summary: The Banovina Palace in Novi Sad, Serbia, is a complex consisting of two buildings. The larger Banovina serves as the seat of the Government of Vojvodina, while the smaller Banski dvor serves as the seat of the Assembly of Vojvodina.

spots.summary: Varadin Bridge is a bridge over the Danube river in Novi Sad, Vojvodina, Serbia. The current bridge built in 2000, replaced the original bridge destroyed during NATO bombardment on 1 April 1999.

spots.name: Statue of Peter I of Serbia in Novi Sad
Prince Tomislav Bridge
spots.summary: Prince Tomislav Bridge was a road bridge on the Danube river in Novi Sad, current day Vojvodina, Serbia. The bridge was opened for traffic on 20 May 1928. The design was inspired by the Liberty Bridge in Budapest, Hungary. It was destroyed on 11 April 1941 by the Yugoslav army during the Invasion of Yugoslavia.

spots.summary: The Greek Catholic Church is a Greek Catholic church in Novi Sad, Serbia. Built in 1847, it is located in Stari Grad at the corner of Jovan Subotić and Svetozar Miletić streets. The church is consecrated to the Holy Apostles Peter and Paul and built in the Pannonian Baroque style.

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Great place to buy very cheap, fresh fruit and vegetables, homemade cheese, and many other things! Highly recommended for anyone who is looking for a true Serbian market experience.
